question: If each unaided attempt to quit smoking has a 4% chance of lasting, what is the percentage chance that at least one of 15 succeeds?
move: A method that rarely works each time can still work eventually.
trap: About 4%, as if one try's odds were a lifetime's odds.
hint: Work out the chance that every single attempt fails.
steps: 0.96 is about e to the −0.04, so fifteen failures ≈ e to the −0.6 ≈ 0.55.
reference: Hughes, Keely & Naud, Shape of the relapse curve and long-term abstinence among untreated smokers, Addiction, 2004
